arxiv-1408-0243.title: Computation of Partially Invariant Solutions for the Einstein Walker Manifolds’ Identifying Equations Journal: Commun Nonlinear Sci Numer Simulat
arxiv-1408-0243.creator: Mehdi Nadjafikhah, Mehdi Jafari
arxiv-1408-0243.description: Abstract In this paper, partially invariant solutions (PISs) method is applied in order to obtain new four-dimensional Einstein Walker manifolds. This method is based on subgroup classification for the symmetry group of partial differential equations (PDEs) and can be regarded as the generalization of the similarity reduction method.

arxiv-2104-05033.title: Mission Design for the TAIJI misson and Structure Formation in Early Universe
arxiv-2104-05033.creator: Xuefei Gong, Shengnian Xu, Shanquan Gui, Shuanglin Huang and Yun-Kau Lau
arxiv-2104-05033.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xuefei Gong, Shengnian Xu, Shanquan Gui, Shuanglin Huang and Yun-Kau Lau. Gravitational wave detection in space promises to open a new window in astronomy to study the strong field dynamics of gravitational physics in astrophysics and cosmology. The present article is an extract of a report on a feasibility study of gravitational wave detection in space, commissioned by the National Space Science Center, Chinese Academy of Sciences almost a decade ago.

arxiv-2110-02268.creator: D. D. Wangsawijaya 1,2, N. Hutchins 1
arxiv-2110-02268.description: Abstract Following the findings in Wangsawijaya et al. 2020 , we re-examine the turbulent boundary layers developing over surfaces with spanwise heterogeneous roughness of various roughness wavelengths 0.32 ≤ S / δ ¯ ≤ 3.63 0.32\leq S/\overline{\delta}\leq 3.63 , where S S is the width of the roughness strips and δ ¯ \overline{\delta} is the spanwise-averaged boundary-layer thickness.

arxiv-2209-11579.creator: Tianchen Shen, Irene Di Giulio, Matthew Howard
arxiv-2209-11579.description: Abstract Human activity recognition has become an attractive research area with the development of on-body wearable sensing technology. With comfortable electronic-textiles, sensors can be embedded into clothing so that it is possible to record human movement outside the laboratory for long periods.

arxiv-2405-07479.title: Enhancing 3D Object Detection by Using Neural Network with Self-adaptive Thresholding
arxiv-2405-07479.creator: Houze Liu 1,†, Cangqing Wang 1,⋆, Xiaoan Zhan 2, Haotian Zheng 3, Chang Che ∗
arxiv-2405-07479.description: Abstract Robust 3D object detection remains a pivotal concern in the domain of autonomous field robotics. Despite notable enhancements in detection accuracy across standard datasets, real-world urban environments, characterized by their unstructured and dynamic nature, frequently precipitate an elevated incidence of false positives, thereby undermining the reliability of existing detection paradigms.

arxiv-2508-21761.creator: Xavier Juanola, Giovana Morais, Magdalena Fuentes, Gloria Haro
arxiv-2508-21761.description: Abstract Visual sound source localization is a fundamental perception task that aims to detect the location of sounding sources in a video given its audio. arxiv-2511-20746.title: Neural Deprojection of Galaxy Stellar Mass Profiles
arxiv-2511-20746.creator: M. J. Yantovski-Barth, Hengyue Zhang, Nolan Smyth, Connor Stone, Martin Bureau, Yashar Hezaveh, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur
arxiv-2511-20746.description: Abstract We introduce a neural approach to dynamical modeling of galaxies that replaces traditional imaging-based deprojections with a differentiable mapping. Specifically, we train a neural network to translate Nuker profile parameters into analytically deprojectable Multi Gaussian Expansion components, enabling physically realistic stellar mass models without requiring optical observations.

pmc-10669937.title: Robotic Distal Pancreatectomy Yields Superior Outcomes Compared to Laparoscopic Technique: A Single Surgeon Experience of 123 Consecutive Cases
pmc-10669937.creator: Hao Ding, Michal Kawka, Tamara M H Gall, Chris Wadsworth, Nagy Habib, David Nicol, David Cunningham, Long R Jiao, Ulrich Friedrich Wellner, Jörg Kleeff
pmc-10669937.description: Simple SummaryPancreatic tumours usually require surgical removal. With advancing technology, these operations can be performed using laparoscopic and robotic techniques, which reduce surgical trauma to patients compared to conventional open surgery. In theory, robotic surgery should yield better outcomes due to its superior precision and control.

pmc-10670290.title: The Usefulness of the Eosinophilic Esophagitis Histology Scoring System in Predicting Response to Proton Pump Inhibitor Monotherapy in Children with Eosinophilic Esophagitis
pmc-10670290.creator: Jovan Jevtić, Nina Ristić, Vedrana Pavlović, Jovana Svorcan, Ivan Milovanovich, Milica Radusinović, Nevena Popovac, Ljubica Simić, Aleksandar Ćirović, Miloš Đuknić, Maja Životić, Nevena Poljašević, Danilo Obradović, Jelena Filipović, Radmila Janković
pmc-10670290.description: Background: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is an immune-mediated esophageal disease with rising incidence. While proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are the first-line treatment, a significant proportion of patients do not respond. This study aimed to determine if the EoE Histology Scoring System (EoEHSS) can predict PPI responsiveness.

pmc-11410798.title: Author Correction: Asymmetry underlies stability in power grids
pmc-11410798.creator: Ferenc Molnar, Takashi Nishikawa, Adilson E Motter
pmc-11410798.description: . The actual parameter values used to generate the figure are b1 ≈ 2.47, b2 ≈ 3.17, b3 ≈ 1.47 (or equivalently, b1 ≈ 1.47, b2 ≈ 3.17, b3 ≈ 2.47). pmc-11505463.title: Prognostic Value of Speckle Tracking Echocardiography-Derived Strain in Unmasking Risk for Arrhythmias in Children with Myocarditis
pmc-11505463.creator: Nele Rolfs, Cynthia Huber, Bernd Opgen-Rhein, Isabell Altmann, Felix Anderheiden, Tobias Hecht, Marcus Fischer, Gesa Wiegand, Katja Reineker, Inga Voges, Daniela Kiski, Wiebke Frede, Martin Boehne, Malika Khedim, Daniel Messroghli, Karin Klingel, Eicke Schwarzkopf, Thomas Pickardt, Stephan Schubert,
pmc-11505463.description: Background/Objectives: Risk assessment in pediatric myocarditis is challenging, particularly when left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is preserved. This study aimed to evaluate LV myocardial deformation using speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE)-derived longitudinal +strain (LS) and assessed its diagnostic and prognostic value in children with myocarditis.

pmc-11710467.title: Precision Phenotyping of Mild Behavioral Impairment and the Early Detection of Dementia
pmc-11710467.creator: Ipsit V Vahia
pmc-11710467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). There is growing recognition of the importance of changes in behavior as an early clinical marker of the onset of Alzheimer’s disease. Behavior symptoms may precede the onset of cognitive symptoms by as many as three years.

pmc-11860289.title: War in Ukraine as a mental health challenge of Czech health care workers
pmc-11860289.creator: M Janoušková, M Kuklová, P Čermáková, J Pekara, J Šeblová, D Šeblová
pmc-11860289.description: IntroductionCzech health care workers recently experienced serious challenges to their mental health. After the COVID-19 pandemic that was extremely stressful, a war in Ukraine caused a flood of refugees that needed health care. Although the Czech Republic does not have borders with Ukraine, it welcomed more than 400,000 refugees in 2022.

pmc-12548957.title: What Can the Running Body Do? The Running Machine's Affective Possibilities and the Limits of Language
pmc-12548957.creator: Jean Ketterling, Bridgette Desjardins
pmc-12548957.description: While others have suggested that action sports offer avenues of escape from neoliberal imperatives like maximizing health and self-regulation, we argue that even the most mainstream of sports—amateur road running—holds similar potential. Using data from 20 “running reflections,” we explore running's everyday affective intensities using Deleuzo-Guattarian theory.

pmc-12582959.title: Comparison of adverse events between intensity-modulated radiation therapy and tomotherapy for early stage breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12582959.creator: Yan Xia, Yan-Cheng Yang, Hang-Qi Ren, Yan-Zun Wang, Qing-Feng Li, Ya-Yuan Yu, Guang-Ran Yang, Yang-ke Li, Kai-Cheng Jin, Qi-Fa Luo, Zhi-Heng Bian, Tian Zeng, Jun-Qing Li
pmc-12582959.description: IntroductionEarly stage breast cancer treated with adjuvant radiotherapy with two different techniques, tomotherapy (TOMO) and intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), and their acute adverse events in terms of skin toxicity, localized edema, sore throat, tracheal mucositis, nausea, oral mucositis, esophagitis, and pneumonitis outcomes are compared.

pmc-12647504.title: The Impact of Intravesical Instillations on Quality of Life in Patients with Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review
pmc-12647504.creator: Ingolf Griebsch, Sunil Shrestha, Yair Lotan, Chi-Fai Ng, Andrew Bottomley
pmc-12647504.description: BackgroundNon-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is commonly treated with transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) followed by intravesical chemotherapy and/or Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) instillations. While these treatments aim to prevent recurrence and progression, the frequency of their administration and associated side effects can substantially impact patients’ quality of life (QoL).

pmc-13077948.title: In silico design of the multi-epitope vaccine for lung adenocarcinoma based on hub gene-derived neoantigens
pmc-13077948.creator: Shaoshuai Li, Minjia Huang, Liqiu Jia, Siyu Liu, Xueting Sun, Daxia Cai, Yanping Su, Minjiang Chen, Chenying Lu, Jiansheng Huang, Jianfei Tu, Jiansong Ji
pmc-13077948.description: BackgroundLung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most prevalent and lethal subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), characterized by an unfavorable 5-year survival rate ranging from 10% to 20%. Neoantigen-based vaccine platforms show encouraging benefits for NSCLC patients. However, the vaccine efficacy may be limited, partially due to low immunogenicity and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.

pmc-13146266.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1126 POTENTIAL PROTECTIVE EFFECT OF ATRIAL FIBRILLATION ON CEREBRAL ATHEROSCLEROTIC STENOSIS: EVIDENCE FROM A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
pmc-13146266.creator: Shumeng Li, Gang Li
pmc-13146266.description: Background and aimsThe association between non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) and cerebral atherosclerosis stenosis is undefined. This study aims to investigate the impact of NVAF on cerebral atherosclerosis stenosis and to analyze independent predictors of atherosclerotic stenosis occurrence in NVAF patients.

pmc-13263741.title: Structural and sociodemographic determinants of BREAST-Q outcomes after gender-affirming breast augmentation in transgender women
pmc-13263741.creator: Daniel S Rouhani, Matthew F McLaughlin, Nina Mehta, Dominick Falcon, Daniel Soroudi, Zuivanna Rivas, Nathan Ramrakhiani, Esther A Kim
pmc-13263741.description: PurposeSociodemographic factors are associated with disparities in postoperative outcomes after gender-affirming surgery, yet their relationship with patient-reported outcomes after gender-affirming breast augmentation remains unclear. We evaluated associations between patient-level and structural factors and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) among transgender women after breast augmentation.

pmc-13280012.title: Anterior Segment Changes after Lens Extraction in Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma Assessed by Scheimpflug Tomography
pmc-13280012.creator: Irem Onal, Elif Ertan Baydemir, Yusuf Yildirim
pmc-13280012.description: PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate changes in anterior segment morphology and intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with acute angle-closure glaucoma (AACG) following early phacoemulsification, using Scheimpflug-Placido disc tomography.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, 32 eyes of 32 phakic patients diagnosed with AACG and referred to a tertiary hospital between 2021 and 2023 were included.

pmc-13545339.title: Comparing the outcomes of the technology‐enhanced learning of sectional anatomy with and without preceding demonstrations: A study about the worked‐example effect in anatomy education
pmc-13545339.creator: Guilherme Reis Borges Coelho Fonseca, George Lim Tipoe, Fraide Augustin Ganotice
pmc-13545339.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The examination of anatomical cross‐sections can facilitate the understanding of spatial and clinical anatomy. Visualization technologies, with dynamic and interactive displays, can be used to learn sectional anatomy in a mostly self‐directed manner. Nevertheless, this study hypothesized that the technology‐enhanced learning of sectional anatomy is improved when initiated with explicit anatomical demonstrations—worked examples, as defined in Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) and Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (CTML).
